ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 11/2021, Ley 6/2023 and Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021), Articles 4 (UBO identification), 14 (identification of promoters and shareholders), 15 and 31 (customer due diligence and reporting); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 182/2017, de 27 de febrero, creating the Registro de Titularidades Reales (UBO register), as modified by Real Decreto 77/2021, de 17 de febrero, transposing EU Directive (UE) 2018/843 (5AMLD); Order PRA/270/2018, de 7 de marzo, on UBO register format and access.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20), general public access to the Spanish UBO register was struck down; disclosure is restricted to competent authorities (SEPBLAC, AEAT), notaries, registrars, and obliged entities performing independent customer due diligence with a legitimate interest.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every promoter, director, authorized signatory, and ultimate beneficial owner against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN List (required due to USD-denominated Swift LC and TT payment rails); and (iv) Spanish domestic databases operated by SEPBLAC and the CNMV. Politically Exposed Persons trigger enhanced due diligence under Articles 14 and 15 of Ley 10/2010, requiring documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis at a minimum UBO threshold of 25%. Any negative hit requires a formal compliance opinion and, where warranted, escalation to SEPBLAC before any incorporation step proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online service of the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org / www.rmc.es) for the certificación negativa de denominación social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the Spanish language; foreign-language names and acronyms must be transliterated into Latin script using Spanish orthography and capitalization rules. The proposed denomination must be legally distinct (unique and not phonetically identical to any existing registered denomination) and must include the designation 'Sociedad Limitada' or the suffix 'S.L.' (alternatively 'S.R.L.').
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the RMC issues a formal negative certificate stating the conflicting existing denomination. The applicant may (i) file a written administrative appeal (recurso) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within one month from notification, attaching the rejection certificate, a certified copy of the applicant's identity, and a legal memorandum on non-conflict; and (ii) simultaneously file a fresh application for up to two alternative denominations at the RMC. The DGSJFP must resolve the appeal within three months; silence is deemed dismissal, in which case judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional may be pursued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A serviced co-working centre or managed business office providing a verifiable physical address in the municipality declared as the registered office may satisfy Articles 9 and 10 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), provided that the administration and management operations align with that address. Pure letterbox or P.O. box addresses are rejected by notaries, the Registro Mercantil, and the AEAT for NIF issuance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 5% probability during the first operating year for a low-risk wholesale trading company, primarily driven by AEAT tax-residency inspections and periodic SEPBLAC CDD compliance reviews rather than unannounced AML physical audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital, arts. 19-34 (constitución, escritura e inscripción), arts. 20-22 (capital social mínimo de la Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada); complemented by Real Decreto 1065/2007 on tax identification numbers and notarial/registry regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office; pre-clearance of the corporate name from the Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de constitución (public deed of incorporation) submitted for first inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Payment is evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit in the company-in-formation account or by notarial deposit; no escrow lock-box is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founder subscribes and fully pays the initial share capital of EUR 3,000, represented by 3,000 participaciones of EUR 1 each, and the allocation of participaciones is approved. (2) The registered office is established at [address], Spain, and is declared the statutory seat for corporate, tax and administrative purposes. (3) [Name] is appointed sole administrator with full powers of representation, including banking, notarial, tax and registry filings. (4) The articles of association are approved. (5) The administrator is authorised to execute all filings with the Mercantile Registry, AEAT, social security, and municipal licensing offices, and to take any corrective steps needed to obtain full legal effectiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain negative certificate of company name from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid, through the electronic portal www.registradores.org
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal application for certification that no existing Spanish company has the proposed name. Provide two or three alternative names. The certificate is a mandatory prerequisite for the notarial deed. Use the registradores.org telematic desk, pay the applicable certificate fee, and collect the signed certification.
required_dossiers: Modelo de solicitud de certificación de denominación social
DNI/NIE or passport of each founding partner
Power of attorney if a representative submits the application
List of two or three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first name is rejected as unavailable or too similar, the second and third alternatives are automatically considered. A reconsideration request may be filed with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month; if the refusal is maintained, select a new distinctive name and re-apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency; electronic headquarters (Sede Electrónica): https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Tax census and VAT registration are managed through Modelo 036 (general registration) or Modelo 037 (simplified registration); customs and export formalities are handled by the AEAT Customs Department (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A Spanish-resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is incorporated by public deed before a notary and registered in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); AEAT assigns a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) before the deed is formalized, followed by the definitive corporate NIF with the 'B' prefix (B + 7 digits + control character). Step 2: A foreign non-resident entity that performs taxable activities in Spain, such as maintaining local warehousing or making taxable supplies, must register in the Economic Activities Census by filing Modelo 036 before commencing operations. AEAT assigns the NIF applicable to the foreign entity's category: an 'N'-prefixed NIF where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment, or the permanent-establishment NIF where a Spanish branch or fixed place of business is created. Step 3: The foreign entity must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain when AEAT requires one for VAT compliance, and must obtain the Spanish VAT identification number, consisting of the NIF prefixed with 'ES' (e.g., ES + NIF), for intra-Community transactions and VIES registration. Step 4: Supporting documents normally requested by AEAT include: certificate of incorporation and registry extract from the home jurisdiction, evidence of foreign tax residence, copy of the public deed and tax representative appointment, power of attorney, and a description of the Spanish fixed establishment or storage operation. Filing is performed electronically using a recognised digital certificate (DNIe, FNMT, or an accepted qualified e-certificate).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxable person under Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Law 27/2014) and is taxed on its worldwide income at the general rate of 25%. The SL is not eligible for pass-through treatment or US-style check-the-box classification; fiscal classification follows the Spanish civil and commercial legal form. Income of a foreign permanent establishment of the SL may be exempt under Article 22 LIS when the foreign branch is subject to a comparable corporate tax of at least 15%; otherwise a foreign tax credit applies. Dividends and interest paid by the SL to non-resident shareholders are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax (IRNR) at the applicable treaty or statutory rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box regime for commercial companies; classification is mandatory and follows legal form. Available statutory elections relevant to this exporting SL: (a) consolidated corporate income tax group election under Article 64 LIS, available to a Spanish parent and its resident subsidiaries where control is at least 75%; (b) VAT group registration (régimen especial del grupo de entidades) for integrated structures with control above 50%; (c) voluntary enrolment in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time VAT bookkeeping system by enterprises below the EUR 24 million mandatory threshold; and (d) mandatory anti-hybrid alignment under the ATAD transposition, under which the Spanish legal form governs the entity's fiscal character and no elective mismatch mechanisms are available for a resident SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax ('IVA' - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 and harmonised with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC. The Canary Islands apply the IGIC (Impuesto General Indirecto Canario) and Ceuta and Melilla remain outside the Spanish VAT territory. Excise duties (Impuestos Especiales) are not applicable to dehydrated vegetables or spices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover exemption threshold in the Spanish VAT general regime: any person or entity carrying out business or professional activities must obtain VAT census registration through Modelo 036 before commencing the activity, irrespective of turnover. The Spanish simplified regime (régimen simplificado), applicable only to enumerated small business sectors with prior-year taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000, does not cover wholesale trading of processed dehydrated vegetable products. The EU-based threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year is relevant solely for intra-Community distance sales of goods and works through the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) when exceeded; this exporter's B2B export model falls outside that threshold framework. Statistical Intrastat thresholds for dispatches of goods to other Member States are updated annually by AEAT and apply when the exporter's intra-EU dispatches exceed the published amount.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Invoices to Spanish public administrations must be issued in Facturae XML format (or an accepted interoperability format) and submitted through the General Entry Point of Invoices (Punto General de Entrada de Facturas). Invoicing software must comply with the anti-fraud requirements of Ley 11/2021 and the Verifactu Regulation (Royal Decree 1007/2023): the software and the resulting invoices must guarantee chronological integrity, generate a chained hash (hash encadenado), and display a QR code on delivered invoices; the taxable person must be able to transmit the invoicing records (Registro de Facturación) to AEAT upon demand. Under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), B2B electronic invoicing between private operators becomes mandatory once the enabling regulation enters into force, with a one-year adaptation period for enterprises exceeding EUR 8 million turnover and a two-year period for other taxpayers. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) quasi-real-time clearance regime is mandatory for enterprises with turnover above EUR 24 million and for VAT groups, requiring transmission of invoice ledger entries to AEAT within four working days of issuance or receipt; for SMEs below the threshold, SII enrolment is voluntary. Export declarations are processed electronically by AEAT's customs system (DUA / Documento Único Administrativo), but no real-time digital stamping of VAT invoices is required for export operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (export exemption with right to deduct input VAT) applies under Article 21(2) of Ley 37/1992 to supplies of dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper that are physically dispatched or transported by the seller, or for the seller's account, to a destination outside the customs territory of the European Union. The essential conditions are: (i) the goods must leave the EU customs territory within the time frame evidenced by the customs export declaration; (ii) the exporter must hold the DUA endorsed by the customs office of departure, the transport document, and, in practice, proof of payment and currency settlement; (iii) the supply must be made under the exporter's Spanish NIF/VAT registration; and (iv) the buyer must be a person established outside the EU, or an indirect-exporter mechanism must be documented. Ancillary services supplied directly to the export goods (freight, handling, inspection, and storage related to the third-country transport) qualify for zero-rating under Article 21(4)-(5) LIVA; B2B services the recipient of which is established outside the EU are located outside the Spanish VAT net under Article 70 LIVA. The zero-rating applies regardless of the Incoterms used, provided the documented transport objective is a destination outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / EX-A Documento Único Administrativo) electronically accepted by Spanish Customs with the applicable TARIC tariff heading for dried vegetables (HS 0712) or crushed/powdered pepper (HS 0904)
Commercial invoice and packing list in Spanish/English, with quantities, unit values, Incoterms and shipping marks matching the DUA
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note) evidencing physical departure from an EU port or airport and arrival at a non-EU destination

Inward Remittance Certificate / export proceeds settlement receipt (justificante de cobro y entrada de divisas) evidencing receipt of the export consideration through Swift LC or TT Wire into the exporter's Spanish bank account
Transport contract, customs forwarding instructions, insurance certificate, and Incoterms evidence (e.g., FOB Valencia or CIF destination)
Certificate of Origin (EUR.1, EUR.MED or non-preferential C/O) issued by the competent Chamber of Commerce where required by the destination market for tariff or documentary purposes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export zero-ratings by cross-referencing the DUA endorsement, the Modelo 303/390 VAT periodic returns, the company's commercial and transport files, and the Banco de España external-transactions statements. If the export is not conclusively proven, the supply is recharacterised as a domestic taxable transaction: the output VAT at 21% is assessed together with statutory late payment interest (interés de demora) and a graduated penalty under Article 191 of Ley 58/2003 (LGT) of between 50% and 150% of the tax deficiency. Defective or missing invoice records fall under Article 201 LGT penalties. The combined evidence of customs declaration, transport title, and banking proof of receipt is the minimum standard expected in both VAT and corporate income tax audits. Although Spanish VAT law does not impose a statutory 180-day repatriation deadline, AEAT treats 180 days as the audit-reasonable benchmark for demonstrating that export proceeds were actually received; a longer collection period must be justified by documented commercial terms. Uncollected or unproven export receivables may be reclassified as domestic sales or intra-Community acquisitions, with reversal of the zero-rating and recalculation of VAT for the whole audit period. Fraudulent export schemes - falsified DUAs, fabricated shipping documents, or circular payment structures - are treated as tax fraud: administrative penalties up to 150% of the tax, asset embargoes, and, where the defrauded amount in one tax period exceeds EUR 120,000, the criminal offence of Article 305 of the Código Penal, carrying imprisonment of one to five years, disqualification, and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated penalties apply where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 600,000 or an organised structure is used; the liability extends jointly to the legal entity, its de facto administrators, and the appointed tax representative in accordance with Spanish liability rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (export exemption with right to deduct input VAT) applies under Article 21(2) of Ley 37/1992 to supplies of dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper physically dispatched or transported by the seller, or for the seller's account, to a destination outside the EU customs territory. The substantive conditions are: (i) the goods must leave the EU within the period evidenced by the customs export declaration; (ii) the exporter must hold the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) endorsed by the customs office, the transport document, and proof of payment; (iii) the supply must be made under the exporter's Spanish VAT registration; and (iv) the buyer must be a person established outside the EU or export must be effectuated through an indirect-export arrangement. Ancillary services directly related to the exported goods (freight, handling, storage, inspection) supplied to a third-country customer may also be zero-rated under Article 21(4) and (5) LIVA, and pure B2B services located to a non-EU customer are outside the Spanish VAT net under Article 70 LIVA. The zero-rating applies irrespective of the Incoterms used, provided the transport documentation demonstrates a non-EU destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / EX-A Documento Único Administrativo) electronically accepted by Spanish Customs, with the correct TARIC tariff line for dehydrated vegetables or crushed/powdered pepper
Commercial invoice and packing list (Spanish/English) matching the DUA quantities, values and shipping marks
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note) evidencing departure from an EU port or airport and arrival outside the EU customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate / export proceeds settlement receipt (justificante de cobro y entrada de divisas) evidencing receipt of funds via Swift LC or TT Wire into the exporter's Spanish bank account
Transport contract, customs forwarding instructions and Incoterms evidence (e.g., FOB or CIF)
Certificate of Origin (EUR.1, EUR.MED or ordinary Certificate of Origin) where required by the destination country to claim preferential or non-preferential tariff treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT verifies export zero-ratings by cross-referencing the DUA endorsement, the Modelo 303/390 VAT summaries, the company's shipping and payment ledgers, and the Banco de España external transactions records. If the export is not conclusively proven, AEAT recharacterises the supply as a domestic taxable transaction: the output VAT at 21% is assessed, plus statutory late payment interest and a graduated penalty under Article 191 of Ley 58/2003 (LGT) of 50% to 150% of the deficient tax; defective documentation may also trigger Article 201 LGT penalties. Although no statutory 180-day repatriation deadline exists under Spanish VAT law, AEAT treats 180 days as the audit-reasonable benchmark for crediting export proceeds; longer terms require documented commercial justification, otherwise the zero-rating may be reversed and the sale treated as domestic or intra-Community. Fraudulent export schemes, including falsified DUAs, fabricated transport documents, or circular payment structures, are prosecuted as tax fraud: administrative penalties up to 150% of the tax, asset embargoes, and, where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single tax period, the criminal offence of Article 305 of the Código Penal carries imprisonment of one to five years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and disqualification. De facto administrators and managers are jointly liable under Spanish tax liability rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (BdE); Foreign exchange and balance-of-payments statistical supervision is shared with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional (SGTFI) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. The regulatory framework is primarily Real Decreto 1816/1991, as amended, and Banco de España Circular 4/2022 on external transactions documentation. AML/KYC supervision is exercised by Banco de España through the Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales (SEPBLAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full member of the euro area; the EUR is freely convertible and capital movements are fully liberalized under Articles 63-66 TFEU and EU Regulation 2019/452. There is no exchange control approval for current account or capital account transactions. Spanish corporate profit remittance restrictions are nil for EU/EEA shareholders, while dividends to non-EU residents are subject to a reduced Spanish withholding tax rate under the applicable tax treaty where a hedge against double taxation is established. The only non-restrictive obligations are statistical reporting duties: any operation with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 (or EUR 10,000 for cash instruments) must be declared to Banco de España. Since the target entity operates in wholesale trade of dehydrated vegetables and spices, it qualifies as routine trade-related capital movement with no sectoral FDI screening trigger.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose any surrender, mandatory conversion, or deemed-repatriation obligation on export proceeds. Export receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be freely retained in domestic or overseas accounts of the Spanish SL. For statistical control, payment receipts from non-resident buyers exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction or aggregated to EUR 50,000 or more in a single calendar year must be reported via the Banco de España external transactions statistical declaration. No conversion ratio or statutory time limit applies to the holding of export proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for supplementary payment rails only. Under PSD2 and Spanish Law 5/2015 on payment services, an EU-licensed electronic money institution (EDEI/EMI) can passport into Spain and provide virtual IBANs, multi-currency accounts, and low-cost FX conversion, which is useful for LATAM/US collections on the dehydrated spices trade. Legal constraints require that such EMI cannot replace a licensed credit institution for export LC confirmation, discounting, documentary credit negotiation, or provision of the statutory corporate payment account linked to the Spanish NIF/CIF that trade counterparties usually require. Banco de España Circular 1/2023 requires the EMI to apply full KYC/UBO identification and to apply the same access-to-obligations screening; an offshore, non-EU EMI must not be used as a primary operating account because such entity lacks MiFID/PSD2 pass-porting rights and creates tax-nexus and withholding-remittance risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law permits fully remote onboarding under Article 9 of the AML Law 10/2010 where the entity is verified through e-IDAS-qualified electronic signature, video-identification, and digital submission of apostilled corporate documents. In practice, Tier-1 Spanish banks impose a de facto requirement: for a newly incorporated SL with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners, at least one managing director must complete an in-person compliance interview at the bank branch and sign the account mandate agreement. For the target entity, the recommended strategy is to appoint a tax-accredited local director with power of attorney, or travel of the non-resident director for one business day to Madrid/Barcelona to satisfy the interview and obtain immediate account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO structure causing beneficial ownership opacity at the 25% threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SL public deed (escritura de constitución), Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation, Spanish NIF/CIF certificate, apostilled passport copies of all UBOs, signed UBO Declaration in the Sepblac format, corporate chart showing each natural person's quota percentage, and source-of-funds evidence in the form of six-months personal bank statements and source-of-wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment concentration on the supplier side, including payments routed through LATAM intermediaries or invoice factoring vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase orders, commercial invoices, bills of lading and weight certificates for dehydrated garlic flakes and chili pepper consignments, packing lists, marine cargo insurance policy, customs SAD/DUA export documents, and an internal counterparty due-diligence file containing the supplier's passport, trade registration, and bank letter confirming the payee is the contract beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hits on any buyer or supplier name in the spice trade network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or LexisNexis screening certificates dated within onboarding week, explanation-of-transaction narrative submitted to the Compliance Committee, country of end-user and end-use certification, and where relevant a clearance opinion from an EU sanctions lawyer demonstrating compliance with EU Regulation 269/2014 and the G7 price-cap regime if such applies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SL with no prior transactional history and a minimal capital balance contrary to the €3,000 SL statutory presumption
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan covering procurement volumes, warehouse contracts, transport framework agreements, three signed purchase orders from US/LATAM/EU buyers, IAE tax census filing under epigraph equivalent to wholesale trade of food products, and an equity injection letter from the shareholders confirming the capital commitment under the Crea y Crece SL en formación sucesiva regime.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The share capital of the Spanish SL must be disbursed by the foreign shareholder from an account held in the shareholder's own legal name via an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire; no third-party gratuitous subrogation is permitted. The MT103 reference field (tag 70) should state 'APORTACION DE CAPITAL / PRIMA DE EMISION' together with the SL's CIF/NIF and the notarial deed date. Operationally, the funds must be credited to the SL's euro-denominated operational account, and the bank should mark the credit as 'capital contribution' to facilitate the subsequent notary certificate of payment (certificado de desembolso) for Registro Mercantil filing. If the cumulative contribution exceeds EUR 50,000 in a calendar year, the SL must submit the Banco de España D-4 foreign investment statistical declaration within one month of the credit; no exchange-control permit or prior authorization is required for non-sensitive wholesale-trade activities, and no minimum capital threshold applies where the SL opts for the en formación sucesiva profile under Law 18/2022, provided the statutory restrictions on profit distribution and loss-related capital increase are observed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the target bulk dehydrated vegetables and spices business, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for direct TT settlements and commercial letters of credit for larger or recurring LATAM and US buyers. A documentary LC must be issued by the buyer's foreign bank and advised by the Spanish SL's account bank through an MT700; once the presentation of invoice, bill of lading, phytosanitary/certificate of origin, and weight/purity certificates meets the LC terms, payment is released and booked as export proceeds via MT754/MT798. For intra-EU supplier payments, clearing should route through SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) settled in TARGET2 and EBA Clearing, while USD-denominated receipts require the Spanish bank's US correspondent account (Fedwire/CHIPS) with the SL's benefit in the SWIFT field 59; full documentation on each outgoing wire must be retained to support the EUR 50,000 statistical declaration duty and VAT export validation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla EUR/USD foreign exchange forward contracts (forwards) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a local Spanish master agreement with a bank counterparty, covering underlying export receivable exposure up to 12 months tenor.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-currency exposures such as the Argentine peso or other LATAM managed-floating currencies, permissible only where the underlying export sales generate inconvertible proceeds and the NDF is entered with a licensed credit institution or authorized broker, with mandatory EMIR trade reporting to a Spanish trade repository as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/MXN) for tenor-matched long-term purchase contracts and for hedging of the fixed pricing on bulk spice supply agreements; these swaps must be collateralized under a Bank of Spain authorized ISDA CSA or local credit support annex and reported under EMIR REFIT obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (for calendar-year accounts, approval by 30 June and deposit by 30 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties per Article 283 LSC: fines range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, depending on delay; if accounts are not deposited for 18 months, the registry closes the company's entry, preventing registration of corporate deeds and triggering administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of Statutory Books (Legalización de libros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year accounts, by 30 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lack evidentiary value in commercial and tax proceedings; fines up to EUR 30,000 may be imposed; tax and accounting documents may be disregarded, leading to added assessments and surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return (Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT – Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-year-end period (for calendar-year companies, 1-25 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharges of 10% plus monthly late-payment interest; after six months surcharge rises to 20%; penalties up to EUR 100,000 or more for willful non-filing; procedural restrictions on government contracts and subsidies; persistent non-filing may trigger enforcement actions but not administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for an S.L. if at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets > EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average headcount > 50. Public interest entities or companies with majority public capital are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable) pursuant to the Commercial Code and amended by Royal Decrees 1514/2007 and 1/2021; aligned with EU accounting directives. IFRS is not mandatory for non-listed companies but may apply to consolidated financial statements of groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain imposes no separate annual UBO confirmation filing for an S.L.; however, the company must maintain an up-to-date internal register of ultimate beneficial owners and report changes to the Mercantile Registry within one month of any transfership. Share transfers must be inscribed in the Register of Members without delay, and the UBO register updated accordingly. The compliance officer should reconcile the UBO register with the annual accounts each year and document confirmation in the board minutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Socios)
General Meeting Attendance Book (Libro de Asistencia)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada may apply a reduced 15% rate on taxable income up to EUR 300,000 for the first two tax years in which they obtain a positive taxable base, provided they perform an actual economic activity. The general 25% rate applies thereafter. No territorial tax holiday applies to a Spanish SL; R&D, export-insurance, bad-debt and stock-valuation deductions are available only under the ordinary law. Tax losses are not subject to a fixed 5-year expiry; Spain permits indefinite carryforward of net operating losses, so the numeric field below is set to 0 as the sentinel for 'no statutory limit.'

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades; submitted electronically via the AEAT Sede Electrónica (electronic tax administration portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year entity, the filing window is 1 July through 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number of the Spanish SL assigned by AEAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL must quote its own NIF; foreign non-resident shareholders have no direct entry in this box. Any Spanish permanent establishment of a non-resident must separately register using NIF-ES with a designated representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year being declared, expressed as a four-digit tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the calendar fiscal year unless an alternate tax period was approved by AEAT; foreign ownership does not alter the entity's fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss for the year before corporate income tax, determined under Spanish GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL reports its full worldwide accounting result. A non-resident parent's consolidation entries or foreign tax provisions are excluded from this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after statutory adjustments, including exemption and participation-relief rules, book-tax differences, and prior-year loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the participation exemption (Art. 21 LIS) here only if the SL's qualifying holding in a non-resident affiliate meets the shareholding and holding-period requirements. Attach supporting parent company ownership details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 565 / Casilla 00565 – Líquido a ingresar / cantidad a devolver
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after quarterly prepayments, withholdings and credits, or the amount refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SL paid dividends, royalties or interest to a non-resident, related withholding tax payments must be made under separate forms (Modelo 123/210/216) and are reconciled through this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 – Pago fraccionado; submitted electronically via AEAT Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 20 calendar days following the end of the accumulated period. For calendar-year SLs, deadlines are 20 April (first quarter), 20 October (first nine months), and 20 December (first eleven months).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year for which the prepayment is made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same fiscal year as Modelo 200; non-resident shareholders have no separate filing obligation in this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Must be marked when the filing is made by a tax representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident parent or agent, only when the Spanish SL is represented by an appointed tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayment amount calculated on the accumulated taxable base using the simplified or rejoinder methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must recognise this as a prepayment of the SL's final corporate tax; it is not a tax on the parent company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted Modelo 202 payments are subject to the same graduated surcharge regime under Article 27 LGT, enforced collection in default cases, and daily late-payment interest; failure to file the return itself carries an additional fixed penalty of EUR 200.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime (IRNR). Exemption applies to dividends paid to qualifying EU/EEA parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 5% of the Spanish SL's capital for a minimum of one year. Treaty rates may reduce the 19% statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double-tax-treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction to the Spanish withholding agent. The certificate must carry apostille or legalisation when required and a Spanish translation. The withholding agent must retain the certificate in its files and reduce the withholding rate only when the treaty entitlement is clearly established. If tax was deducted at source at 19%, the non-resident can file Modelo 210 with the AEAT and obtain a refund, attaching the residence certificate, evidence of beneficial ownership, and a statement from the Spanish entity confirming the payment. EU Directive relief is claimed by furnishing the same residence documentation and the relevant related-entity holding declaration; refunds or exemptions are processed through the non-resident tax return process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding for royalties paid to non-residents is 19%; interest on qualifying debt instruments also carries a 19% withholding rate. Under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive, interest and royalties paid to an EU associated company holding at least 25% of the Spanish company for two years are exempt. Treaty rates typically reduce interest to 5%–10% and royalties to 5%–10%; for example, Spain–United States applies 10% on interest and 10% on royalties. The reduced treaty rate must be applied only after formal acceptance of the residence certificate and beneficial ownership declaration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Modelo 232 annual related-party reporting are triggered when the aggregate amount of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 in a fiscal year. A Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated worldwide net turnover reaches EUR 75 million. Transactions with tax-haven jurisdictions are subject to lower de minimis thresholds and must always be documented.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulation; instead, it applies the OECD-aligned substance-over-form doctrine through Article 15 LIS (anti-abuse), Article 100 LGT (fraud of law), and the CFC rules of Article 100 LIS. A Spanish SL engaged in bulk dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper export must maintain demonstrable local substance: real office or warehouse, locally resident management, operational contracts, payroll, business correspondence, financial accounts, and commercial risk. Beginning January 2019, letterbox companies lacking economic substance may be disregarded, income re-attributed, and treaty benefits denied where management and control are effectively exercised abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting export revenues from Modelo 200, overstating purchases of dehydrated vegetables, using false invoices, recording non-existent costs, or concealing foreign bank accounts where the amount of tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per fiscal year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount, loss of subsidies and public procurement rights, and public conviction disclosure. The AEAT additionally imposes a civil tax penalty of 50%–100% of the unpaid tax plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director who participates, orders, consents, or negligently fails to supervise the evasion is criminally responsible. Directors may be personally imprisoned and ordered to pay civil restitution; the corporate veil is pierced to attach personal assets, and travel bans, passport surrender, and seizure of director bank accounts may be imposed during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no local office, no employees, no independent judgement, no operational control, and no commercial risk, while all substantive actions and decisions for the dehydrated spice export are carried out by a non-resident parent or intermediary, with no real local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT recharacterises the arrangement under the general French anti-abuse doctrine, applies CF, and detrives treaty benefits; the taxable base is recalculated at the 25% corporate rate, plus a 50% penalty, late interest, and additional surcharges. The arrangement may be re-qualified as a permanent establishment of the foreign entity, triggering additional non-resident taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who allow the company to function as a pure shell are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts under Articles 42.2 and 43 LGT. Liability extension includes personal bank accounts, vehicles, and real property; criminal proceedings may result in imprisonment for tax evasion, and a travel ban can be issued to secure the director's presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File, Master File, or Modelo 232 related-party return when annual related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000; failing to price the purchase and sale of dehydrated garlic, chili powder, or spices at arm's length; or deriving margins inconsistent with a distributor or commissionaire.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to provide required TP documentation triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 1,500 per omitted or inaccurate data item, with a minimum penalty of EUR 5,000. If the absence of documentation prevents the AEAT from confirming the arm's-length result, an additional tax adjustment is made with a 50% surcharge on the tax difference. Recidivism elevates the sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs the Modelo 200 or who knowingly fails to produce TP evidence can be declared jointly liable for the corporate tax adjustment under Article 42.2 LGT. In serious cases of false documentation, criminal liability for falsification of accounts or fraud may be pursued, with possible imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the beneficial owner of the Spanish SL, accepting cash payments above EUR 2,500 from another entrepreneur in connection with spice export transactions, failing to maintain a proper transfer trail, or omitting to report suspicious wire transfers linked to trade payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 10/2010: minor infractions up to EUR 60,000, serious infractions from EUR 60,000 to EUR 150,000, and very serious infractions from EUR 150,000 up to EUR 5,000,000. Separate tax penalties and seizure of undeclared cash are imposed for concurrent tax offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Spanish SL are 'obliged subjects' under Spanish AMLA. Directors who personally breach KYC, registration, or reporting duties are individually fined. Criminal money-laundering convictions under Article 301 of the Criminal Code carry 6 months to 6 years imprisonment and confiscation of assets; travel bans and passport suspension are commonly ordered.
